runs.entry: Price **$46.95** a share (close 2026-10-16 through `tools/run.py`, aggregator, flagged). Shares **133,741,067** common at 2026-07-31 (10-Q cover, accession 0001124198-26-000071; repurchased shares cancelled, no treasury count; 135,564,463 issued and outstanding at 2026-06-30 used for the per-share arithmetic because net cash is taken at that date). Sovereign **5.43%** (US Treasury 30-year par, 2026-10-16). Filings read: the 10-K for FY2025 (0001124198-26-000007) and its 10-K/A (0001124198-26-000025), the 10-Q of 2026-08-07, the proxy of 2026-03-12, the 8-Ks of 2026-04-23 and 2026-08-07, the 10-Ks FY2019 to FY2024 (FY2019 filed late after an NT 10-K), NuScale's own filed operating cash 2021 to 2024; operating cash FY2025 $(387)M cross-checked against the filed statement. The brief's stated departure: lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7; competitors the 10-K names (KBR, Jacobs and AECOM read; Bechtel, Kiewit, Black & Veatch and the international firms flagged as not SEC filers; Amentum, also named, not chosen, declared under contamination). **Q1 IN**: engineering and construction work sold on clients' capital projects with little fixed capital, 81% of backlog reimbursable; the level of earnings not foreseeable (the filer's own "unpredictable" awards), the shape and the competitive position foreseeable; the doubt row recorded as contrary evidence. **Q2 OUT**: no part above half of five-year segment profit, Urban Solutions the largest at 36.9% and deciding, Energy Solutions read as well (largest without the $643M Santos reversal); the filer's own "non-traditional competitors offering below-market pricing" and "downward pressure on our contract prices and profit margins", lump-sum work lost if "our bid is higher than the competition", no pricing power through the inflation (cost growth on infrastructure projects, $255M of backlog on legacy projects in a loss position), new awards $19.5B, $15.1B, $12.0B over 2023 to 2025; operating margin 2017 to 2025 in aggregate Fluor -0.1% against KBR 6.4%, Jacobs 4.6% and AECOM 4.0% (company facts, not checked line by line), the lowest of the four in eight of nine years. Q3 to Q12 not reached. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash (operating cash less capital spending, stock pay and payouts to minority partners, NuScale's consolidated burn added back, interest on cash removed) **$61.3M** a year over 2016 to 2025, the ten-year cycle base central because 2025 carries Santos; the literal 2021 to 2025 window $3.6M ($132.0M with Santos added back); divestiture proceeds excluded from owner cash and counted in net cash (CONVENTION of the run); sales decline carried as the bottom (CONVENTION of the run); net cash $2,113M (10-Q at 2026-06-30 plus the Mexico joint-venture sale it states); value range **$22.55 to $23.91** a share all-equity against $46.95 (literal window $16.00 to $16.08, most generous base $30.57 to $33.52); no case earns the floor (enterprise value $4,252M would need about $425M a year at no growth); fair **$19.79 all-equity** ($5.05 equity-only, which values the cash only through its interest); not armed, the box is not OUT at Q7 or IN. Balance sheets 2016 to June 2026: retained earnings down about $2.9B from 2017 to 2021, equity $3,125M to $1,030M by 2020, Stork's goodwill ($532M at 2016-12-31) impaired and sold away, equity rebuilt in 2024 by the NuScale fair-value gain, part of net cash held in joint ventures and restricted. Facts after the stop, recorded not judged: the FY2019 10-K filed late with 2016 to 2018 restated and the filer's own finding that former Energy & Chemicals leaders "caused pressure to be applied" to present "overly optimistic forecasts"; the SEC's $15M civil penalty of 2023; a new class action of 2025 and a 2026 NuScale shareholder suit naming Fluor; the 2025 bonus measure excluding large litigation costs (Santos), the CEO paid $1.33M of incentive in a year of a $51M net loss; buybacks at about $42 to $49 a share with no stated price limit, above the computed range, $1.4B targeted for 2026. Contamination declared by the analyst: a date-filtered `Test Runs/` listing showing the AMTM and ARCAY run and folder names, and the AMTM commit subjects in the session's git context; none opened, none used. Commits 3b4ce064 (template), 2dac5292 (Step 0 and Q1), e1741f77 (Q2), 58466b23 (computation, box, close). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Citations: the analyst's `check_ids.py` clean; the dispatcher's `dispatcher_cite_check.py` 40 ids, no missing id, no E-id, 53 fragments, three flags verified clean by hand (two regex captures of the run's own prose beside L2004-003, whose row holds "most insureds don't care from whom they buy" and "price competition in insurance is usually fierce"; one curly apostrophe against the shelf's damaged character in M2013-086): **no slip**. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) Q1 against Q2 for a contractor whose yearly level is unforeseeable and whose shape is plain, a Q1 TOO HARD (NATURE) or a Q1 IN that Q2 closes, two analysts could split; (2) Q7 (b) on an owner-cash series that crosses zero, whether a decline in another filed series may set the bottom; (3) Q7 (c) with divestitures and no purchases, whether proceeds count; (4) the operating losses of a consolidated investee later sold (NuScale); (5) the equity-only figure read beside the all-equity figure for a company holding large net cash; (6) the template asks for the balance sheets in Step 0 and gives Step 0 no slot. Could not get: NuScale's stock pay and pre-2021 burn inside Fluor's figures, operating leases (not read), a line-by-line check of the rivals' figures.
runs.narr: OUT at Q2 after Q1 IN (Fluor Corporation; NYSE FLR; EPC and project management in Urban Solutions, Energy Solutions and Mission Solutions, NuScale sold and Stork divested). No part above half; Urban Solutions (36.9% of five-year segment profit) decides and Energy Solutions is read beside it. The castle is open on the filer's own words: below-market pricing by new entrants, downward pressure on prices and margins, lump-sum work lost to the lower bid, no pricing power through the inflation, new awards falling from $19.5B to $12.0B over 2023 to 2025; operating margin 2017 to 2025 -0.1% in aggregate against KBR 6.4%, Jacobs 4.6% and AECOM 4.0%, the lowest of four in eight of nine years. Computation beneath the stop: owner cash $61.3M a year on the ten-year base, value $22.55 to $23.91 all-equity against $46.95, no case earns the floor, fair $19.79 ($5.05 equity-only), not armed. Facts recorded, not judged: the late FY2019 10-K and restatement with forecasts pressured by former Energy & Chemicals leaders, the SEC's $15M penalty, new suits, a bonus measure excluding Santos, buybacks above the computed range. No citation slip. Framework gaps for the operator: Q1 against Q2 for a contractor, a cash series crossing zero, divestitures without purchases, a sold consolidated investee's losses, the equity-only figure with large net cash, the template's Step 0 slot.
